title: Build Verification Lab — System Overview
description: The lab takes a project directory, runs it through syntax → run → tests, and records an honest verdict.
body: The Automated Build + Verification Lab is the system's quality gate. Given a project directory — typically fresh output from the generator — it checks every JavaScript file with node --check, executes the entry file with an 8-second timeout, runs any declared tests, and returns a stage-by-stage report with a final pass boolean and an earned verification status. The demonstration runs the lab's own demo project: syntax pass, run pass, test pass, status tested. A failing project is demonstrated too — recorded as failed, never hidden.

t: Stage 1 — Syntax: node --check on Every File

title: Stage 2 — Run: Execute the Entry File
t: Stage 2 — Run: Execute the Entry File

title: Stage 3 — Tests: Declared Expectations Checked
description: Each test runs a command and passes only on exit 0 plus the expected output substring.
body: Tests are not vibes: command, exit code, expected output. The demonstration runs the lab's test stage with a squares-of-3 test and prints the per-test result with the captured output.

title: Failure Is Recorded, Not Hidden
description: A broken program produces a recorded failure with the real error — the lab never pretends it passed.
body: The lab's credibility rests on this record. The demonstration verifies the lab's deliberately broken demo project — a ReferenceError at runtime — and prints the real report: pass false, run stage failed, status demoted to generated, and the captured ReferenceError text. Failures are data, and the lab treats them that way.

title: Fix and Re-Run — The Redemption Loop
t: Fix and Re-Run — The Redemption Loop
description: A fixed project re-verified: fail → fix → pass, with both reports on record.
body: Verification is a loop, not a stamp. The demonstration writes the broken project, verifies it (fail), overwrites the entry with the working version, verifies again (pass), and prints both verdicts — the exact fix-and-reverify cycle the master relies on.

title: Report Format — What a Verdict Contains
t: Report Format — What a Verdict Contains
description: Every verdict carries per-stage results, pass counts, and the earned verification status.
body: The report shape is fixed: ok, project_dir, stages array (each with stage name, pass boolean, and details), stages_passed count, overall pass, and verification_status. The demonstration prints the lab's stage list from the live program.

title: Timeout Protection — Infinite Loops Are Killed, Not Waited On
t: Timeout Protection — Infinite Loops Are Killed, Not Waited On
description: Any stage exceeding 8 seconds is terminated and recorded as timed out.
body: A hung program must not hang the lab. The demonstration verifies a project whose entry loops forever; the run stage kills it at the timeout and records timed_out true with pass false — the real behavior of the live code.

title: Limits and Honest Boundaries
description: The lab verifies Node.js programs locally; it cannot test browser behavior, networks, or other languages.
body: Plain limits. The lab runs node --check and node execution — it cannot verify a web page renders, a network call succeeds, or a Python program behaves. Unsupported test commands are recorded as failures, not skipped silently. The demonstration runs a test with an unsupported command and prints the honest recorded failure.

title: Audit Trail — Every Verdict Is Reproducible Evidence
t: Audit Trail — Every Verdict Is Reproducible Evidence

body: A verdict is evidence, not a thumbs-up. The demonstration verifies the demo project and prints the audit keys present on the verdict object — proving the report carries everything needed to re-examine the result without re-running it.
